name: Lady Million Empire
remarks: Checked Oct 2026. Pyramid confirmed by Lookfantastic, Perfume Loft, Hnak and Perfumania (orange, neroli, red currant / magnolia, orange blossom, osmanthus, mirabelle / cognac, patchouli, white musk). Year 2019 by Hnak and Perfumania; EDP by Lookfantastic, Perfume Loft and Hnak; perfumers Anne Flipo and Jean-Christophe Hérault (IFF) by Perfume Loft and Hnak. Flanker of Lady Million. Current availability not verified. New note: Mirabelle Plum.

name: Fève Délicieuse
remarks: La Collection Privée Christian Dior. Dior describes it around Venezuelan tonka bean absolute and Madagascar vanilla, with bergamot and rose; caramel comes from Olfastory and retailers, not from Dior's own list. Still listed on dior.com (page seen via search, direct fetch blocked).

name: Eau Belle
remarks: Pyramid from Osmoz (peach skin listed as Peach). Olfastory gives a different split (top mandarin, bergamot, lemon, coriander; heart yuzu, neroli, cyclamen, freesia; base white musk, cypress). Jadof also lists seringa in the heart. Perfumer only from Olfastory. Likely discontinued but not confirmed.

name: Diorissimo Eau de Toilette
remarks: Pyramid from Osmoz. Olfastory adds rosewood (top), orange blossom and ylang-ylang (heart); Wikipedia mentions ylang-ylang, boronia, amaryllis and jasmine. Reformulated for IFRA (Wikipedia). 1956 is the original launch; EDT is the reference version. Current EDT availability not directly confirmed. New note: Amaryllis.

name: Courrèges in Blue
remarks: Original 1983 pyramid (Luxsure). Relaunched in 2014 as Eau de Parfum, reformulated by Nadège Le Garlantezec (Givaudan); Osmoz lists the 2014 version as floral aldehydic with ginger, galbanum / lavender, floral notes / patchouli, sandalwood. Auparfum credits Edouard Fléchier for the original and classes it chypre. Current availability not verified.

name: Kenzo World Power
remarks: Flanker of Kenzo World (2016), unrelated to Kenzo Power (2008). Described as a salty-sweet oriental; official pyramid has one note per tier. Likely discontinued, not confirmed.

name: So Scandal!
remarks: Flanker of Scandal. Jasmine is sambac. Brand lists only a milky accord in the base (no specific material); raspberry appears on Olfastory but not in the brand's short list. Year confirmed by Wikipedia. Likely discontinued, not confirmed.

name: Angel Muse
remarks: Flanker of Angel. Olfastory gives top grapefruit, pink pepper / heart hazelnut / base vetiver, patchouli, vanilla; Osmoz gives heart red fruits and base cocoa, vanilla, patchouli, vetiver, hazelnut (no top). Merged here. Likely discontinued, not confirmed.

name: Black XS L'Excès for Him
remarks: Flanker of Black XS. Osmoz lists it as Eau de Parfum; some retailers sell it as eau de toilette, so concentration is slightly uncertain. Ozonic accord with smoky-woody cypriol (nagarmotha) heart. Likely discontinued, not confirmed.

name: Luna
remarks: Part of Les Belles de Nina. Pyramid from retailer (wild berries mapped to Forest Fruits, tangerine to Mandarin). Olfastory lists top lemon, orange blossom and no pear, and tags it unisex, while it is marketed for women. Likely discontinued, not confirmed. New note: Immortelle.

name: Santal Royal
remarks: Not L'Art et la Matière: it belongs to Les Absolus d'Orient, now sold as Absolus Allegoria. Pyramid from Guerlain's official page (seen via search, direct fetch blocked). Still sold.

name: L'Homme Libre
remarks: Flanker of L'Homme. Note placement varies: Osmoz puts nutmeg, rose-bay, bergamot on top and violet, star anise, basil in heart, base patchouli, vetiver, leather; Olfastory and retailers put bergamot, basil, star anise on top and nutmeg, violet leaf (plus pink pepper) in heart, base vetiver, amber woods, patchouli. Likely discontinued, not confirmed.

name: Patchouli Blanc
remarks: Olfastory classes it oriental/chypre, Wikiparfum woody/ambery. Amber added from Wikiparfum's flat list. Wikiparfum marks it discontinued while Nocibé still lists a 'Dolce Riviera - Patchouli Blanc' EDP page; status unclear. Perfumer only from Olfastory.

name: Empreinte
remarks: Courrèges' first perfume (Firmenich). Olfastory pyramid (aldehydes, bergamot / rose / oakmoss, patchouli, castoreum) completed with notes from the 2012 relaunch listing (mandarin, jasmine, sandalwood, vetiver, leather). Reformulated for the 2012 relaunch (animal materials) and again reissued in 2021 with a simpler bergamot/patchouli/ambroxan structure. Olfastory tags it unisex; originally marketed for women. One source dates it 1970.

name: Burberry Body
remarks: Osmoz and Olfastory pyramids match. Osmoz family Chypre Floral. Likely discontinued, not confirmed. New note: Absinthe (wormwood).

name: Oud Essentiel
remarks: Not L'Art et la Matière: part of Les Absolus d'Orient, now Absolus Allegoria. Guerlain's pyramid (pelargonium = Geranium, Atlas cedarwood) matches Olfastory. Launch year 2017 from Olfastory only (Guerlain page gives none). Still sold.

name: Cerruti 1881 pour Femme
remarks: Checked Oct 2026. Year 1995 confirmed by Osmoz, Vesira and Fragazon; EDT by Vesira and Fragazon; Claire Cain credited by Fragazon (and Olfastory) only among sources reached. Cerruti's own page confirms the flax-flower signature with light woods. Pyramids differ: Osmoz gives bergamot, green notes / violet, narcissus, rose, tuberose / vanilla, sandalwood, flax; Vesira gives mimosa, freesia, bergamot, violet / orange blossom, chamomile, geranium, jasmine, rosewood, flax / sandalwood, amber, musk, cedar. Current pyramid merges them, so it is marked inferred. New note: Flax Blossom.

name: In Love Again
remarks: Created for YSL's 40th anniversary. Pyramid from Selfridges (muscat grape as Grape). Olfastory gives a different list: grapefruit, plum, grape / rose, green notes, black currant, raspberry / white musks, sandalwood, cedar. Perfumer and year confirmed by Wikipedia. Likely discontinued, not confirmed. New note: Grape.

name: Fidji
remarks: Checked Oct 2026. Joséphine Catapano (IFF) confirmed by Wikipedia FR, Eau de Tati and Australian Perfume Junkies. 1966 is given by all three as the creation date; Wikipedia's infobox gives 1973 as the launch year, so 1966 means composition. Pyramid confirmed by Eau de Tati (galbanum, ylang / jasmine, rose, tuberose, clove, iris / ambergris, musk, patchouli, sandalwood); carnation from Australian Perfume Junkies. Green floral chypre. Reformulated over time (now L'Oréal); believed still sold, not formally verified.

name: Alien Essence Absolue
remarks: Checked Oct 2026. Year 2012 and Dominique Ropion confirmed by Osmoz, The Candy Perfume Boy and Now Smell This. Sold as Eau de Parfum Intense (refillable 30 and 60 ml per NST). Pyramid confirmed by all three: sambac jasmine, heliotrope, orris, cashmeran, myrrh, white amber, vanilla. Olfastory's different pyramid (orange blossom, anise) not followed. Candy Perfume Boy calls it softer and less diffusive than Alien, with dry vanilla and incense. Likely discontinued, not confirmed.

name: Fuel for Life Homme
remarks: Diesel's first fragrance with L'Oréal (Wikipedia). Some retailers class it oriental woody. Still listed by retailers; Diesel US site lists a 50 ml format.

name: Pi
remarks: Stylized π. Year and perfumer confirmed by Wikipedia; notes from Olfastory only, which gives no heart notes (mentions an 'Infinium' accord). Second note source not found (search budget exhausted, retailer pages blocked). Believed still sold, not verified.

name: Armani Code Profumo
remarks: Flanker of Armani Code. Despite the 'Profumo' name, Osmoz and Olfastory list it as Eau de Parfum (not Parfum). Olfastory top: mandarin, apple, bergamot. Some retailers list leather in the base. Possibly replaced by later Code flankers; availability not verified.

name: Rem
remarks: Single source only (Olfastory); description also mentions calone and fenugreek. Could not find an independent second source (search budget exhausted, Osmoz has no page). Believed still sold, not verified.

name: Ysatis
remarks: Checked Oct 2026. Year 1984 and Dominique Ropion confirmed by Wikipedia, Bois de Jasmin and Undina (Ropion also by Perfume Shrine; Undina says it was his first commercial fine fragrance). Bois de Jasmin lists citrus, galbanum, aldehydes, rose, tuberose, patchouli, vanilla, sandalwood and mentions moss; Perfume Shrine adds mandarin and clove. Sources also cite ylang-ylang, jasmine, narcissus, coconut and civet, absent from the current pyramid. Reformulated: modern version fresher on top with milder moss and less animalic base (Bois de Jasmin, Perfume Shrine).

name: Kokorico
remarks: Checked Oct 2026. Year 2011 confirmed by Wikipedia, The Candy Perfume Boy, CaFleureBon and Persolaise; EDT by Candy Perfume Boy and Persolaise; Annick Ménardo and Olivier Cresp by Candy Perfume Boy and CaFleureBon. Notes agree (fig leaf, cocoa, patchouli, vetiver, cedar) but placement differs (Candy Perfume Boy puts cocoa in the base), so tiers are inferred. CaFleureBon and Candy Perfume Boy both say the late ambrox/woody drydown turns synthetic. Kokorico by Night followed in 2012. Likely discontinued, not confirmed.

name: Rumeur
remarks: 2006 Rumeur, not the 1934 Lanvin Rumeur. Pyramid from Osmoz (seringa/mock orange; ambroxol read as Ambroxan) plus lily of the valley from retailers. Wikiparfum classes it chypre floral and marks it discontinued. New note: Mock Orange.

name: Parisienne
remarks: Year and Grojsman credit confirmed by Wikipedia; notes and co-perfumer Sophie Labbé from Olfastory only. Likely discontinued, not confirmed.

name: Champs-Élysées
remarks: Perfumer conflict: French Wikipedia and Olfastory credit Jean-Paul Guerlain, English Wikipedia credits Olivier Cresp and calls it a mimosa floral. French Wikipedia says a new composition was created in 2021 (reformulated/relaunched). Notes from Olfastory only.

name: Deci Delà
remarks: Single source (Olfastory), which lists Eau de Toilette, not the Eau de Parfum named in the batch list; EDP existence not verified. No independent confirmation of year, perfumer or notes found (search budget exhausted). Likely discontinued, not confirmed.
